args.reason: Check current on-hand, reserved, quarantined, damaged, and usable stock levels for SKU-1005 at NODE-BOG-F5.
Check existing purchase orders for SKU-1005 to see if supply is already inbound or overdue.
Check recent sales history, stockout days, promotions, and forecast demand to evaluate daily burn rate and stockout risks.
Check available supplier options and potential expedite options for open purchase order PO-505.
Check available budget, storage space capacity, and autonomy spending limits for purchasing decisions.
Simulate all candidate plans to evaluate projected baseline and alternate purchasing or expediting options against demand and inventory constraints.

assumptions: Forecast demand of 100 units/day will continue as modeled over the 28-day planning horizon.
important_factors: The recommended purchase of 800 units is infeasible as it costs $12,000.00 from SUP-A (or $14,000.00 from SUP-B), exceeding the available budget limit of $10,000.00.
Baseline simulation shows a 4-day stockout starting 2026-09-27 with a total of 400 unmet units prior to the arrival of open order PO-505.
Expediting open purchase order PO-505 (2,000 units from SUP-A) by 4 days to 2026-09-27 completely eliminates the stockout (0 residual unmet units).
Expediting PO-505 incurs an incremental fee of $450.00, which is feasible within the $10,000.00 budget and storage capacity (60 m³ peak occupancy vs 200 m³ capacity).
The $450.00 expedite fee exceeds the buyer autonomy limit of $250.00, requiring buyer approval.
args.rationale: The system recommendation to buy 800 units is rejected. Simulation shows an 800-unit PO is infeasible because it costs $12,000.00 from SUP-A or $14,000.00 from SUP-B, exceeding the available budget of $10,000.00. Furthermore, an 800-unit order is unnecessary to prevent stockouts. Current usable inventory is 1,000 units, and daily forecast demand is 100 units/day. The baseline projection indicates stock runs out on 2026-09-27, leading to a 4-day stockout totaling 400 unmet units before open order PO-505 (2,000 units) arrives on 2026-10-01. Expediting existing purchase order PO-505 by 4 days to arrive on 2026-09-27 resolves the shortage entirely, leaving 0 residual unmet units at an expedite fee of $450.00. This is far more cost-effective than placing a new purchase order ($7,000.00+). Because the $450.00 fee exceeds the $250.00 autonomy expedite fee limit, this action is submitted for buyer approval.
